subject: Consolidated console signal: cost/latency sample-rate and exception policy
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 19 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: unified cost/latency signal + sampling exceptions for console tiles

Hi Rachel / Ben,

Quick heads-up: Acme (pilot) flagged cases where the console's per-route cost tile underreported tail latency during batched inference. They want a single, explainable "signal" we can publish that aligns cost attribution with latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) and that supports exception rules (canary models, debug routes).

I sketched a short proposal attached (console-proposal-v1.pdf) and a sampling matrix for how we'd collect additional spans without blowing quota (sampling-matrix.csv). Key asks:
- Product: agree on acceptance criteria for the new signal (what constitutes "aligned").
- Infra/Runtime (Ben): feasibility of adding a sampled span at the request router with preserved KV cache context.
- Console UX (Rachel): how this maps to current tiles and drill path (owner/permissions).

Can we do a 30-min sync this week? Suggested agenda in the doc.

Thanks,
Kimberly

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: console-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 19 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: unified cost/latency signal + sampling exceptions for console tiles

Kim / Rachel — thanks for the write-up, Kim. Quick thoughts after a skim:

- Sampling: we can add a lightweight sampled span at the load-balancer level, but two trade-offs: increased tracing ingest and potential KV-cache context loss if the span is forwarded across a different pod. The sampling-matrix.csv you attached is useful; we should baseline ingestion delta across three sample rates (0.1%, 1%, 5%).
- Canary/exceptions: we can tag canary requests via routing metadata and exclude/include them in the consolidated metric. That part is straightforward today.
- Backfill: for historical alignment (customer ask), we can't retroactively reconstruct P99 without traces. We can approximate with request logs + token counts but will call out accuracy limits in the acceptance criteria.

I added two suggested engineers to the meeting list: Lina (infra-runtime) and Omar (tracing). If possible, I can run a quick ingest delta test Tues morning.

Ben
Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sampling-matrix.csv (sample sizes / ingest delta estimates)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Zhao <lina_zhao@redwood.com>, Omar Malik <omar_malik@redwood.com>, Acme Analytics <eng@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 20 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: unified cost/latency signal + sampling exceptions for console tiles

Thanks Kim and Ben — good framing. I set up a 30-min slot and a short agenda (agenda-console-sync.md) to keep this focused:

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: recap of customer ask (Acme) and pain (Kim)
- 10m: infra feasibility & sampling delta (Ben + Lina)
- 5m: console mapping + drill expectations (Rachel)
- 5m: acceptance criteria + rollout plan (all)
- 5m: decision & owners / JIRA follow-up (SUP-4567)

Proposed meeting: Tue Jul 20, 11:00–11:30 PT (calendar invite sent). Lina / Omar — can you confirm viability of a 1% sample pilot and whether we can preserve KV cache correlation on sampled spans? Ben: if you can run the ingest-delta test Tues morning that'd be perfect; we'll review results in the sync.

Acme — looping you in; we may ask for a short example trace or two to validate. If you prefer, you can upload anonymized traces to the shared doc (link below).

Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-console-signal-proposal
JIRA: SUP-4567 (console: unified cost/latency signal)

Thanks — looking forward to a concise decision so we can scope UX work.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Console Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: agenda-console-sync.md

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lina Zhao <lina_zhao@redwood.com>, Omar Malik <omar_malik@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics <eng@acme-analytics.com>, CloudMarketOps <pm@cloudmarket.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 21 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: unified cost/latency signal + sampling exceptions for console tiles — meeting notes + next steps

Thanks everyone for the quick sync. Notes and decisions below (short and actionable):

Decisions:
- Pilot sample rate: 1% across non-canary traffic for 2 weeks (Ben / Lina to run ingest delta test and confirm resource impact by EOD Wed).
- Canary handling: include canary as explicit tag; by default we will not roll canary into tenant-level aggregated signal (but provide a toggle in the UI).
- Backfill: we will provide an approximation layer for historic P95/P99 using request logs; marked as "estimated" in console.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Ben: run ingest-delta test at 1% and 5% and post results to SUP-4567 by 2027-07-21 EOD. (attachment: sampling-matrix.csv)
- Lina / Omar: confirm KV-cache correlation preservation for sampled spans or propose workaround by 2027-07-22.
- Rachel: prototype a drill flow wireframe and set up a short UX review with CS (target 2027-07-25).
- Kim: update the proposal doc with decision language, acceptance criteria and exceptions policy; push to Drive (done).

Risks / notes:
- If ingest increases >15% at 1% sampling, we'll revert to 0.5% for pilot and expand sampling windows for spikes only.
- Customer validation: Acme will share two production traces (anonymized) and a list of routes they consider high-cost/high-latency.

Attachments: console-proposal-v1.pdf, sampling-matrix.csv
JIRA: SUP-4567
Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-console-signal-proposal

Kimberly
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
